meta.basis: Place list and categories follow the Wikipedia article 'Tourism in West Bengal'. Descriptions are short and general. Railway links are marked by how well we could source them; see each place's rail.confidence.

categories.name: Hill stations and treks
categories.blurb: Himalayan foothills and ridge walks in North Bengal.

categories.name: Sea and beaches
categories.blurb: Bay of Bengal beaches in the south of the state.

categories.name: Religious and pilgrimage
categories.blurb: Temples, mosques, churches, gurdwaras, monasteries and Jain sites.

categories.name: Wildlife and national parks
categories.blurb: Tiger reserves, mangroves, rhino and elephant forests.

categories.name: Heritage and architecture
categories.blurb: Palaces, terracotta temples, colonial buildings and old capitals.

categories.name: Culture and city life
categories.blurb: Literary, artistic and everyday Kolkata and Bengal.

places.name: Darjeeling
places.summary: Hill station known for tea gardens, mountain views and the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

rail.stationNote: Nearest main railhead, then a road journey of a few hours. The toy train runs from Siliguri/NJP.
rail.note: Howrah has a Howrah–New Jalpaiguri line, and Sealdah has trains to New Jalpaiguri (for example the Darjeeling Mail). Neither runs to Darjeeling itself, so you change to road or the toy train.

places.name: Kalimpong
places.summary: Quiet hill town with monasteries, orchid nurseries and colonial buildings such as Morgan House.

rail.stationNote: Nearest main railhead, then a road journey.
rail.note: Reached by changing at New Jalpaiguri, which both Howrah and Sealdah connect to by direct trains.

places.name: Sandakphu and Singalila
places.summary: The state's highest point, at 3,636 m per the Wikipedia page, reached by a ridge trek in Singalila National Park.

rail.stationNote: Then road to Manebhanjan, where the trek starts.
rail.note: Via New Jalpaiguri, then road.

places.permit: National park rules, fees and guide requirements apply. Confirm with the West Bengal Forest Department.

places.name: Kurseong
places.summary: Small hill station between Siliguri and Darjeeling, listed among the state's hill stations.

rail.stationNote: Road from Siliguri; the toy train line also passes through.
rail.note: Via New Jalpaiguri, then road.

places.name: Mirik
places.summary: Lake and hill town, listed among the state's hill stations.

rail.note: Via New Jalpaiguri, then road.

places.name: Lava, Loleygaon and Rimbick
places.summary: Small, quieter hill villages listed on the page among North Bengal hill stations.

rail.note: Via New Jalpaiguri, then road.

places.name: Digha
places.summary: The best-known beach resort of the state, mainly visited by domestic travellers.

rail.note: The Howrah station page shows Digha only as a station on a route map and does not say Howrah trains serve it. We could not confirm a direct service from Howrah or Sealdah, so check IRCTC.

places.name: Mandarmani
places.summary: Beach settlement listed on the page. The page notes that some beaches here are firm enough to drive cars on.

rail.station: Contai Road or Egra (nearest main stations; confirm locally)
rail.note: We have not confirmed the nearest station or which Kolkata terminal has direct trains.

places.name: Shankarpur and Tajpur
places.summary: Quieter beach settlements listed on the page.

rail.note: Not confirmed.

places.name: Bakkhali and Gangasagar
places.summary: Coastal settlements in the delta. Gangasagar is also a major pilgrimage site, especially at Makar Sankranti.

rail.station: Namkhana (for Bakkhali area) and Kakdwip region
rail.stationNote: Sealdah's southern suburban lines run to Namkhana, then road and ferry.
rail.note: The Sealdah station page lists lines to Kakdwip and Namkhana and a Ganga Sagar Express to Jaynagar. Ferries and road complete the journey.

places.name: Dakshineswar Kali Temple
places.summary: Major Kali temple on the Hooghly, known for its idol of Goddess Bhavatarini.

rail.stationNote: On the Sealdah main line route via Dum Dum and Baranagar.
rail.note: The Sealdah page lists a Sealdah–Dum Dum–Baranagar–Dakshineswar route.

places.name: Kalighat Kali Temple
places.summary: One of the four Adi Shakta pithas, per the Wikipedia page, in south Kolkata.

rail.stationNote: Reached by city metro and road rather than long-distance train.
rail.note: A city destination: arrive at Howrah or Sealdah, then use metro, taxi or app cab. We have not mapped exact connections.

places.name: Belur Math
places.summary: Headquarters of the Ramakrishna Mission on the Hooghly, listed among the state's Hindu sites.

rail.stationNote: On the Howrah suburban network and close to Howrah.
rail.note: Belur Math is in Howrah district, but the Howrah and Sealdah station pages do not mention it, so we could not confirm a direct train. Check IRCTC or local transport.

places.name: Mayapur (ISKCON)
places.summary: Large ISKCON temple complex listed among the state's Hindu sites.

rail.note: The Sealdah page lists Sealdah–Krishnanagar services, and Krishnanagar is in the same district. Final road leg not mapped.

places.name: Tarapith
places.summary: Shakta pitha listed on the page, in the Birbhum district.

rail.note: The Sealdah station page lists a Maa Tara Express to Rampurhat, the nearest main station. A direct Howrah service was not confirmed from the Howrah page.

places.name: Murshidabad: Nizamat Imambara and Katra Mosque
places.summary: The page describes the Nizamat Imambara as the largest in India and Bengal. Katra Mosque is also listed.

rail.note: The Sealdah page lists Sealdah–Krishnanagar–Berhampore–Lalgola and a Bhagirathi Express to Lalgola. A Howrah link was not confirmed.

places.name: Bandel Church (Basilica of the Holy Rosary)
places.summary: Historic church at Bandel, listed on the page under Christianity.

rail.stationNote: Bandel is a junction on the Howrah suburban main line.
rail.note: Bandel is not mentioned on the Howrah or Sealdah station pages we read, so we could not confirm a direct connection. Check IRCTC.

places.name: Kolkata: St Paul's Cathedral, St John's Church, mosques and gurdwaras
places.summary: Kolkata has churches (St. Paul's Cathedral, St. John's, St. James), the Tipu Sultan Shahi Mosque, several gurdwaras and Jain temples, all listed on the page.

rail.station: Howrah or Sealdah, then city transport
rail.note: Both Howrah and Sealdah are main Kolkata terminals; use metro, taxi or app cab from there.

places.name: Darjeeling monasteries (Ghoom, Bhutia Busty and others)
places.summary: The page lists Ghoom Monastery, Bhutia Busty Monastery, Mag-Dhog Yolmowa, Tharpa Choling and Zang Dhok Palri Phodang as Buddhist sites in the hill region.

rail.station: New Jalpaiguri (NJP), then road or toy train
rail.stationNote: Ghoom is also a station on the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway.
rail.note: Via New Jalpaiguri.

places.name: Pakbirra Jain temple
places.summary: Jain temple site in Purulia listed on the page.

rail.note: Not confirmed.

places.name: Sundarbans National Park
places.summary: A UNESCO World Heritage mangrove forest, tiger conservation area and Biosphere Reserve.

rail.note: The Sealdah page lists Sealdah–Canning and Namkhana lines. A Howrah link was not confirmed.

places.permit: Entry needs a permit from the forest authorities. Book through an authorised operator.

places.name: Jaldapara, Gorumara and the Dooars
places.summary: Forest parks in North Bengal. Gorumara is noted for the Jatraprosad watch tower views.

rail.station: Hasimara, New Mal, Alipurduar or New Jalpaiguri
rail.note: The Sealdah station page lists trains to New Alipurduar and Alipurduar. The Howrah page lists a Howrah-New Jalpaiguri line but does not mention Alipurduar, so a Howrah link was not confirmed.

places.permit: Park rules and seasonal closures apply.

places.name: Buxa Tiger Reserve
places.summary: Tiger reserve in North Bengal listed on the page.

rail.note: Sealdah has trains to New Alipurduar and Alipurduar.

places.permit: Reserve rules apply. Confirm with the forest department.

places.name: Neora Valley National Park
places.summary: Described on the page as one of the richest biological zones in the Northeast.

rail.note: Via New Jalpaiguri.

places.permit: Permission is usually needed to enter. Confirm with the forest department.

places.name: Victoria Memorial and the Maidan
places.summary: Iconic marble memorial and museum, named on the page as a Kolkata landmark and one of the state's seven wonders.

rail.station: Howrah or Sealdah, then metro or road
rail.note: Both terminals are in Kolkata. Use metro, taxi or app cab to the Maidan area.

places.name: Howrah Bridge (Rabindra Setu)
places.summary: Famous bridge over the Hooghly, named as a Kolkata landmark and one of the state's seven wonders.

rail.stationNote: The bridge ends at Howrah station.
rail.note: The bridge links Kolkata and Howrah, and Howrah Junction is at its western end. This is general geography rather than a statement from the station page.

places.name: Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden
places.summary: Botanic garden at Shibpur, home to the Great Banyan Tree. The page says it is the oldest and largest of its kind in Southeast Asia.

rail.note: Located in Shibpur, Howrah district.

places.name: Bishnupur terracotta temples
places.summary: Temples known for their terracotta work, one of the state's seven wonders on the page.

rail.note: The Howrah station page shows a Sheoraphuli–Bishnupur branch via Tarakeswar but does not say Howrah trains run directly. Check IRCTC for current trains.

places.name: Hazarduari Palace, Murshidabad
places.summary: Three-storey palace and ASI museum, noted on the page for its large chandelier and staircase.

rail.note: Via the Sealdah–Krishnanagar–Berhampore route.

places.name: Cooch Behar Palace
places.summary: Palace built in 1887 and modelled on Buckingham Palace, per the page.

rail.station: Cooch Behar or New Cooch Behar
rail.stationNote: Part of the North Bengal rail network.
rail.note: Not confirmed which Kolkata terminal has direct trains.

places.name: South Park Street Cemetery
places.summary: British-era cemetery listed on the page.

rail.station: Howrah or Sealdah, then metro or road
rail.note: Both terminals are in Kolkata.

places.name: Kolkata
places.summary: State capital, called the 'City of Palaces' on the page, with colonial buildings, food and festivals.

rail.station: Howrah, Sealdah, Shalimar, Santragachi and Kolkata stations
rail.stationNote: The page names these as the five intercity stations serving Howrah and Kolkata.
rail.note: Both Howrah and Sealdah serve the city directly.

places.name: Shantiniketan
places.summary: Place linked with Rabindranath Tagore and Visva-Bharati University.

rail.note: Neither the Howrah nor the Sealdah station page mentions Bolpur or Shantiniketan, so we could not confirm which Kolkata terminal has direct trains. Check IRCTC.

places.name: Jorasanko Thakur Bari
places.summary: Tagore family residence in north Kolkata that attracts visitors, per the page.

rail.station: Howrah or Sealdah, then metro or road
rail.note: Both terminals are in Kolkata.

places.name: Kumartuli
places.summary: North Kolkata potters' quarter where clay idols are made. The page counts it among Kolkata's seven wonders.

rail.station: Howrah or Sealdah, then metro or road
rail.note: Both terminals are in Kolkata.

places.name: Eden Gardens
places.summary: Cricket stadium listed on the page.

rail.station: Howrah or Sealdah, then metro or road
rail.note: Both terminals are in Kolkata.
